learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic principles of computer-aided design and operation of mechanisms used in mechanical and mechatronic engineering.
Understands the kinematic characteristics of mechanisms with bars, gears, cams, as well as associated dynamic phenomena.
Knows methods for balancing, efficiency calculation, and geometric optimization of mechanisms.
Is familiar with the stages of structural design and kinetostatic analysis of mechanisms.
Ability to analyze the movement of mechanism elements using graphical and analytical methods.
Correct application of mathematical relations for determining kinematic parameters.
Use of specific software for simulation and modeling of mechanisms.
Design functional solutions for simple and complex mechanisms.
Assuming responsibility in the correct application of design and analysis principles.
Respecting technical and functional requirements in mechanism realization.
Active contribution to solving technical problems within team projects.
Ability to identify and select the appropriate type of mechanism for a technical application.
Developing independent solutions for optimizing mechanism operation.
Autonomous management of the learning process and deepening knowledge in the field.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the science of mechanisms and machines. Basic concepts, kinematic elements, kinematic pairs, kinematic chains, mobility of mechanisms, structural analysis.

Bar linkage mechanisms. Kinematic analysis of planar mechanisms. Kinematic analysis of spatial mechanisms. Kinetostatic analysis. Self-locking of mechanisms. Elements of dimensional design of mechanisms. Examples.

Gear mechanisms. General concepts. Classification. Transmission ratio. Parallel axis gears: external cylindrical gears with straight and helical teeth; internal cylindrical gears. Elements of geometric and kinematic design. Concurrent axis gears. Crossed axis gears: helical gears; worm gears. Mechanisms with gears with mobile axes. Complex gear mechanisms.

Cam mechanisms. Classification of cam mechanisms. Kinematic analysis. Kinetostatic analysis. Elements of cam mechanism design: criteria for choosing motion laws; determining basic geometric parameters; designing the cam profile.
Dynamics of mechanisms and machines. Dynamic models. Phases of machine operation. Mechanical efficiency. Balancing of mechanisms. Regulation of machine movement.
Structural analysis of bar and cam mechanisms.
Kinematic analysis of bar and cam mechanisms.
Structural and kinematic analysis of fixed-axis gear mechanisms.
Structural and kinematic analysis of mobile-axis gear mechanisms.
Generation of involute profile for cylindrical gears.
Calculation of geometric elements for cylindrical gears and gear trains.
Dynamic analysis and balancing of rotors with concentrated masses.
Balancing of rotors on balancing machines.
Determination of efficiency for a worm gear.
Determination of efficiency for a cylindrical gear train.
Defining functional requirements (project work).
Structural design (project work).
Dimensional design (project work).
Kinematic analysis (project work).
Kinetostatic analysis (project work).
Verifications and optimizations (project work).
Technical documentation and conclusions (project work).
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result considers the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades range from 1 to 10, with a minimum passing grade of 5 required to certify the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and grant ECTS credits. The Exam component (50% of the final grade) consists of a formative assessment (40% of the exam component) and a summative assessment (60% of the exam component). A minimum mark of 5 is required for the Exam, Laboratory activities, and Project components. All laboratory works must be completed, allowing for only one make-up session for a missed laboratory work.
